# Legacy Markit Environmental Registry — public view contract

**Hand-written from live measurement on 2026-07-29.** Not generated by
`verra discover`: there is no JSON API here to capture, and Playwright would
record a page load rather than a contract. The page *is* the contract.

Host: `https://mer.markit.com/br-reg/public`
Adapter: `src/carbon_scraper/registries/markit/api.py` (+ `tables.py`)
Registry using it: **Plan Vivo V4** (`registries/planvivo/v4.py`)

---

## What this is

The registry S&P inherited with IHS Markit, still live and still the only
publisher of a great deal of pre-2025 data. It is a server-rendered JSP
application with jQuery and Bootstrap — no SPA, no API, no `robots.txt`
concerns beyond politeness, and no authentication on the public view.

It is a **platform, not a registry**: one view serves 21 programmes behind a
`standardId` parameter. The programme list is published in the page's own
`<select id="public-search-registry">`:

| standardId | Programme |
|---|---|
| `100000000000002` | ISO 14064-2 |
| **`100000000000004`** | **Plan Vivo** |
| `100000000000007` | Social Carbon |
| `100000000000008` | ACRE Carbon Standard |
| `100000000000009` | Climate, Community and Biodiversity |
| `100000000000010` | New Zealand Permanent Forest Sink Initiative |
| `100000000000026` | NZ Projects to Reduce Emissions (Pre 2008) |
| `100000000000027` | No Established Standard |
| `100000000000037` | Pacific Carbon Standard |
| `100000000000130` | Peru REDD+ Program |
| `100000000000003` | Energy Efficiency |
| `100000000000006` | COTE: Willamette: Water Quality (Temperature) |
| `100000000000038` | BEF Flow Restoration Standard |
| `100000000000014` | COTE: Willamette: Wetland Habitat |
| `100000000000015` | COTE: Willamette: Salmonid |
| `100000000000016` | COTE: Willamette: Upland Prairie Habitat |
| `100000000000021` | No Established Biodiversity Standard |
| `100000000000022` | Oregon Wetlands Regulatory (Ratios) |
| `100000000000023` | USFWS Conservation Banking |
| `100000000000056` | W+ Standard for Women's Empowerment |

Only Plan Vivo is ingested today. Adding another is a subclass and a settings
entry — but read "Traps" first, and check what the programme actually
populates before reusing Plan Vivo's column map.

---

## Requests

### The record lists

```
GET /br-reg/public/index.jsp
    ?entity=<entity>
    &standardId=<id>
    &start=<n>
    &sort=<column>&dir=ASC
    &srd=false&entity_domain=Markit
    &acronym=&additionalCertificationId=&categoryId=&unitClass=&name=
```

Every parameter is sent, empty-valued rather than omitted, because that is
what the page's own form submits and this platform's family has form when it
comes to treating an unrecognised request as an unfiltered one.

`entity` is one of — the app's own spellings, including the odd one:

| our ledger | `entity` | sort column |
|---|---|---|
| projects | `project` | `project_name` |
| `issuances` | `issuance` | `account_name` |
| `holdings` | `holding` | `account_name` |
| `retirements` | `retirement` | `account_name` |
| `cancellations` | **`Cancelled`** | `account_name` |

Also present in the tab bar and not used: `account`, `assignment`,
`apiRetirement`.

### The detail pages

```
GET /br-reg/public/project.jsp?project_id=<id>
GET /br-reg/public/master-project.jsp?project_id=<id>
```

Two of them, and which one applies is decided by the link the listing row
carries. A grouped project's rows link to `master-project.jsp` and the id in
that link is the **master's**, shared by every sub-project under it.

### Bulk export — exists, not used

```
POST /br-reg/PublicViewReportDownload.action?responseType=excel|pdf
```

The page builds this form in `downloadReport()` with fields `sort`, `dir`,
`acronym`, `additionalCertificationId`, `categoryId`, `name`, **`standard_id`**
(snake_case here, `standardId` on the GET — worth noticing), `unit_class`,
`responseType`, `entity` and `srd`. Field guesses so far answer HTTP 500
`Requested resource has not been found`. Worth returning to for a large
programme, since a server-side export beats pagination; unnecessary for Plan
Vivo V4 at three pages.

---

## Response

HTML. The records are a `<table>` with a `<th>` heading row.

**Projects** — `Name`, `Category`, `Standard Name`, `Project Type`, `Status`,
`PIUs Listed`, `Validator`, `Developer`, `Country`, `Details`.

**Issuances** — `Vintage`, `Project`, `Account`, `Standard`, `Project Type`,
`Verifier`, `Units`, `Measurement`, `Type`, `Details`.

**Retirements** — `Retirement Date`, `Vintage`, `Project`, `Account`,
`Beneficial Owner`, `Standard`, `Project Type`, `Retirement Quantity`,
`Measurement`, `Type`, `Details`.

No record states an id in any column. The only place a key appears is the
`href` behind the row's "View" link, which is why the parser keeps links
beside values.

---

## Traps

Every one of these was measured, and every one produces output that looks
right.

### `limit` is accepted and ignored

The form posts `limit=15`. Asking for 100 or 500 returns **15 rows, HTTP 200,
byte-identical response**. Third registry in this codebase to accept a
parameter it does not apply, after Verra's filters and Gold Standard's
`project_id`. There is no page size to tune. Do not add one.

### The pager never says stop

There is no total anywhere: no header carries a count and `<li id="page_no">`
renders **empty**. And "Next →" is never disabled — `start=240` against a
35-row feed answers HTTP 200 with an empty table and *still offers a next
page*. A loop that trusts the pager makes 2,000 requests and exits clean.

**Paging ends on an empty page.** That is the only end-of-list this view
states honestly.

### `standardId` is a request, not a filter

Asking for Social Carbon (`100000000000007`) returns retirement rows whose
`Standard` column reads **"No Established Standard"** — because Social Carbon
is an *additional certification* here, not a primary standard, and its
projects are registered under other standards. Whatever the parameter means,
it does not mean "only this standard's rows".

Every row is therefore checked against the `Standard` column this side.
`MarkitPublicAPI.standard_names` is that check, and a programme that omits it
gets whatever the server felt like sending.

### Some `<tr>`s are not records

A merged project emits a second row whose fourth cell carries a **malformed
`style` attribute that has swallowed an entire data payload**:

```html
<td style="34.914551Sofala Community Carbon Project…Active…100000000000169…">
```

Parsed positionally that is a row full of plausible values in the wrong
columns. A record is recognised structurally instead: it carries a "View" link
**in its own cells**, not one inherited through a `rowspan`.

### `rowspan` carries down

A project registered under two standards renders two `<tr>`s where the second
omits the merged cells — no name, no developer, no country — and every
remaining cell slides left. Read positionally, that row's `Category`
("Carbon") lands in the project-name column. The parser resolves merged cells
to their original column index; see `tables.py`.

### A project id is not unique

- **Sofala** (`100000000000169`) renders twice, identically.
- **Scolel té** (`95`) renders twice with *different* project types, because
  its two rows are two sub-projects sharing one `master-project.jsp` id.
- **Olympic Forest** (`103000000017396`) renders as "(Mali)" and "(Senegal)"
  under one id.

`project_id` is half the primary key of `projects`, so rows sharing one are
merged rather than left to overwrite each other: distinct project types are
joined, the row count lands in `extra.mergedRows`, and the alternative names
in `extra.names`. **35 rows are 30 projects.**

### The Country column carries the state — and ISO commas

One cell holds `"<country>, <state>"`: `Viet Nam, Kon Tum`. But several ISO
3166 names contain a comma of their own — `Bolivia, Plurinational State of,
Cochabamba` is one country and one state, and `Korea, Republic of` is a
country with **no** state. Splitting on the last comma is right for the first
and invents a place for the second. `markit.COMMA_COUNTRY_NAMES` is the guard.

### `name` is not a project search

It narrows — `name=zzzznotathing` returns nothing — so it passes the usual
"prove the filter does something" check. It fails the harder one. On the
issuance feed, `name=N'hambita` returns **Mikoko Pamoja** rows, a different
project entirely, and `name=Sofala` returns none of Sofala's own issuances.

Counting rows would have called this a working filter. **Do not partition on
it.** `dir=DESC` does work, and is the one proven way to reach the far end of
a feed if a real depth limit ever appears.

### Ledger rows have no id

Nothing in a ledger row is a key, so `entity_id` is hashed from the row's own
values plus an occurrence index — hashed so the upsert stays idempotent, and
indexed because two rows can be identical in every published column and two
identical events are two events. The registry name is in the hash, so a Markit
key cannot collide with the S&P `entityId` of the same registry's V5 rows.

---

## Politeness

Same as everywhere else: ~1 req/s, on-disk response cache, browser
`User-Agent` (this host wants one too), and this registry's own
`Origin`/`Referer` rather than the shared Verra ones. A full Plan Vivo V4 sync
is roughly 40 requests.
